name: Ransomware containment
description: Contain an in-progress or just-detected ransomware event on an endpoint or identity. Triage the originating signal; if confirmed, isolate the affected host (EDR primary, network ACL fallback), revoke the implicated identity and its active sessions, verify the latest known-good backup snapshot, and drive a notification step that pages the IR lead, the comms officer, and drafts the NIS2 Article 23 early-warning pre-notification within the 24-hour clock. CACAO v2 + SecOps-NG content-model extensions. Forward-public artifact: detection bindings reference upstream SigmaHQ rule IDs only; SecOps-NG does not re-author Sigma rules.

__signal_id__.description: Identifier of the originating detection signal (EDR alert, Sigma match, or SOC-raised ticket).

__affected_host__.description: Host identifier (hostname or asset id) implicated by the signal; consumed by isolation.

__affected_identity__.description: Identity principal (user or service account) implicated by the signal; consumed by identity revocation.

__ransomware_confirmed__.description: Whether triage promoted the signal to a confirmed ransomware event. False routes to close-out without containment.

__edr_available__.description: Whether the EDR agent on the affected host is reachable and capable of issuing an isolate action. False triggers the network-ACL fallback.

__latest_known_good_snapshot__.description: Identifier of the most recent backup snapshot that pre-dates the event window. Produced by the backup-verification step.

__snapshot_integrity_ok__.description: Whether the located snapshot's integrity hash matches the value recorded in the backup catalogue.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: triage signal
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Receive the originating detection signal and hydrate it with host, identity, and process context. Decide whether the signal is a confirmed ransomware event or a benign / out-of-scope alert. Produces __affected_host__, __affected_identity__, and __ransomware_confirmed__.

if-condition--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00.name: ransomware confirmed?
if-condition--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00.description: Branch on __ransomware_confirmed__. True paths into containment; false closes the incident out with no further action (the close-out itself is logged for the false-positive KPI by an out-of-scope card).

if-condition--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00.name: EDR available?
if-condition--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00.description: Branch on __edr_available__. True uses the EDR isolate action; false falls back to a network ACL deny at the operator's egress chokepoint. Both branches converge on identity revocation.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: endpoint isolation — EDR isolate
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Issue the EDR-vendor isolate action against __affected_host__ via the operator's pre-bound EDR agent. Bounded by the operator-supplied authorisation policy. Primary path.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: endpoint isolation — network ACL deny (fallback)
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: EDR fallback: deny all ingress/egress for __affected_host__ at the operator's network chokepoint (firewall rule, switchport disable, or SDN policy). Used when the EDR agent is unreachable or absent.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: identity revocation
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Disable the implicated user account, revoke active sessions, and invalidate refresh/access tokens at the operator's IdP. Includes Kerberos TGT invalidation where supported. Targets __affected_identity__.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: backup verification
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Locate the most recent known-good backup snapshot that pre-dates the event window and verify its integrity hash against the backup-catalogue record. Produces __latest_known_good_snapshot__ and __snapshot_integrity_ok__. Does NOT restore — restore is a separate, out-of-scope recovery playbook.

action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: comms plan
action--30000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Notify the IR lead and comms officer along the operator's pre-bound channels, and draft the regulator early-warning pre-notification per NIS2 Article 23 within the 24-hour clock from initial detection. The drafted notification is staged for human sign-off, not auto-sent. Because this step is the handoff point that closes the incident timeline and trips the statutory reporting clocks, it stamps the timeline-completeness KPI alongside the notification-SLA KPI and the regulator-notification-overrun KRI.
